claim.text: The struck vehicle became a hazard by entering the ego lane.
Perception took 0.12 s from hazard onset to first detection, below the 0.30 s perception threshold.
The handoff decision occurred 4.43 s after first detection.
Only 0.72 s remained from handoff to impact, below the 1.50 s human perception-response time.
Brake actuation took 0.14 s from CAN brake request to pressure reached, below the 0.25 s actuation threshold.
The CAN brake request occurred after the video impact time.
With nominal perception 0.20 s, command 0.05 s, and brake tau 0.15 s, the counterfactual simulation produced no contact and a minimum gap of 49.61 m.
The witness recheck agreed with the original witness that the other vehicle's brake lights were illuminated.
The brake log was complete for the decision window.

The primary contributing factor was the late handoff: the handoff-to-impact margin was 0.72 s, less than the 1.50 s human perception-response time, while the nominal-timing counterfactual avoided contact.
